reading: Each isolated marker shoots diagonal lines in all four diagonal directions to the grid border; a line cell takes the colour of the marker that sits in the same background-stripe colour as that cell.
verb: draw diagonal rays recoloured by region

slots.sources: isolated marker cells (one per stripe colour)
slots.direction: all four diagonals, to the border
slots.colour: per cell: the colour of the marker lying in a stripe of the same underlying colour (region colour -> marker colour key)

why: every changed cell lies on a diagonal through a marker and its new colour is key(underlying stripe colour)

reading: The 3x3 input is placed at the top-left of a 6x6 canvas and every coloured cell is extended down-right diagonally to the canvas border in its own colour.
verb: draw diagonal trails on doubled canvas

slots.canvas: output twice the input size, input at top-left

why: output cell (y,x) equals the input cell (y-k,x-k) for the smallest k>=0 giving a non-background cell

reading: Only the middle column is kept; every coloured cell off the middle column becomes background.

new_rows.name: offmid
new_rows.datalog:
wmax(max(X)) :- px(Y, X, C).
midcol(X) :- px(Y, X, C), wmax(M), D = X + X, D = M.
offmid(Y, X) :- cell(Y, X, C), !midcol(X).

why: all non-background cells outside the centre column become 0; the centre column is unchanged

reading: Each 3x3 bracket attached to a long 0-coloured rail slides along its rail to the rail's far end at the opposite border, carrying whatever is inside it; the rail is erased. Loose 9s not in a bracket stay.

slots.subject: bracket (3-cell-deep cup of 0 plus its contents) at the grid edge
slots.path: the 0 rail extending from the bracket's closed side
slots.target: the far end of the rail at the opposite border
slots.rest: rail cells become background 7; other cells kept

why: each bracket with contents reappears unchanged in orientation at the far end of its rail; rail removed

reading: In every row or column that has a 4 at both grid-border ends, the cells between the two 4s swap colours 0<->8 and 6<->7.

new_rows.name: lane
new_rows.datalog:
hmax(max(Y)) :- px(Y, X, C).
wmax(max(X)) :- px(Y, X, C).
vlane(Y, X) :- px(Y0, X, 4), Y0 = 0, hmax(H), px(H, X, 4), px(Y, X, C), Y > 0, Y < H.
hlane(Y, X) :- px(Y, X0, 4), X0 = 0, wmax(W), px(Y, W, 4), px(Y, X, C), X > 0, X < W.
lane(Y, X) :- vlane(Y, X).
lane(Y, X) :- hlane(Y, X).

why: key is 0->8, 8->0, 6->7, 7->6 on lane cells (bg included); all other cells unchanged

reading: Around every isolated 1 a fixed plus is stamped: 2 above, 7 left, 6 right, 8 below (clipped at the border).
why: each marker gets the identical 3x3 plus (centre 1) and nothing else changes

reading: The interior of the 2-coloured rectangular frame is filled with 2, except the bounding box of the 5 cells, which stays as it is.
verb: fill frame around box of spots

new_rows.name: gap
new_rows.datalog:
osize(O, count(Y, X)) :- obj(O, Y, X).
big(max(N)) :- osize(O, N).
frm(O) :- osize(O, N), big(M), N = M.
fy0(min(Y)) :- frm(O), obj(O, Y, X).
fy1(max(Y)) :- frm(O), obj(O, Y, X).
fx0(min(X)) :- frm(O), obj(O, Y, X).
fx1(max(X)) :- frm(O), obj(O, Y, X).
bgc(Y, X) :- px(Y, X, C), !cell(Y, X, C).
inner(Y, X) :- bgc(Y, X), fy0(A), fy1(B), fx0(P), fx1(Q), Y > A, Y < B, X > P, X < Q.
spot(Y, X) :- cell(Y, X, C), obj(O, Y, X), !frm(O).
sy0(min(Y)) :- spot(Y, X).
sy1(max(Y)) :- spot(Y, X).
sx0(min(X)) :- spot(Y, X).
sx1(max(X)) :- spot(Y, X).
inbox(Y, X) :- inner(Y, X), sy0(A), sy1(B), sx0(P), sx1(Q), Y >= A, Y <= B, X >= P, X <= Q.
gap(Y, X) :- inner(Y, X), !inbox(Y, X).

why: every background cell inside the frame but outside the 5s' bounding box becomes 2; nothing else changes

reading: The output is a fixed 3x3 glyph in colour 5 chosen by the input's single colour: 1 -> plus, 2 -> T (top bar, stem down), 3 -> corner (right column and bottom row).

slots.key: the one non-background colour of the input

why: output depends only on the input colour; each colour always gives the same glyph

reading: The input holds T-tetromino shapes pointing up or down. The output is a 3x6 tally: the left 3x3 half shows the number of stem-up shapes as 3s on corner slots, the right half shows the number of stem-down shapes as 1s.

slots.objects: T shapes of colour 2 (3-cell bar plus 1-cell stem; diagonal touching does not merge them)
slots.classes: stem up -> colour 3, left half; stem down -> colour 1, right half
slots.layout: count n on corner slots of a 3x3 half: 1 -> TL; 2 -> TL,BL; 3 -> TL,TR,BL; 4 -> all four corners

why: number of 3s equals the stem-up count and number of 1s equals the stem-down count on every pair

reading: Each grid has one or more complete multi-coloured template shapes; elsewhere a few cells of a template appear as fragments, and each fragment is completed into the full template at the matching position.

slots.fragments: small cell groups whose colours and relative positions match a part of one template
slots.placement: the template position that makes the fragment cells coincide with the template cells

why: every added cell belongs to a full template copy aligned to the fragment it completes
